background_notes.fact: For a mean-zero Fourier H^gamma datum Q with gamma>0, symmetric truncations converge to Q in L2 and H^gamma. The displayed e(n) has L2 norm one and dot H^gamma norm (n+1)^gamma; it is orthogonal in both norms to p(n). Consequently the defined Qpad(n) has exact homogeneous norm R, L2 norm at most R and tends to Q in L2.

The norms are the supplied nonnegative Fourier series.

background_notes.justification: The two nonzero coefficients of e are 1/sqrt(2) at ±(n+1); p has support |k|<=n. The squared norm therefore splits into two nonnegative contributions and the padding contribution in dot H^gamma is exactly d(n)^2. Since 0<=d(n)<=R, its L2 size is at most R(n+1)^(-gamma), which tends to zero for gamma>0. The remaining error is a tail of a convergent norm series. The square root is legitimate because truncation cannot increase the norm.

background_notes.fact: A continuous Hilbert-space path with norm at most K almost everywhere on [0,T], T>0, has that bound everywhere. If mean-zero L2 paths W_n converge to W uniformly in time and ||W_n(t)||dotHgamma<=K for every n,t, then ||W(t)||dotHgamma<=K for every t.

background_notes.justification: A strict violation of the norm bound persists by continuity on a relative interval of positive measure, including at either endpoint, contradicting the almost-everywhere bound. Each Fourier coefficient is a continuous linear functional on L2, with absolute value bounded by the L2 norm. At fixed t each finite weighted sum therefore converges from W_n to W and stays at most K^2. The supremum over expanding finite frequency sets is the full nonnegative norm series. Neither assertion exchanges an uncontrolled infinite limit.

background_notes.fact: A smooth periodic datum lies in every Fourier H^s. If one source flow is continuous into every finite Sobolev order and satisfies the source polynomial evolution, it is spatially and temporally smooth.

background_notes.justification: Repeated integration by parts in the periodic Fourier integral bounds coefficients by arbitrarily high inverse powers. In the other direction, Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the absolute sum of the jth differentiated Fourier series by the H^s norm times (sum_k <k>^(2j-2s))^(1/2), finite when s>j+1/2. This gives continuous spatial derivatives and their time continuity. The evolution expresses the time derivative as a polynomial of spatial derivatives; differentiating this identity repeatedly gives all mixed derivatives. All required higher-order flows are supplied by E001, so this is only the routine final smoothness deduction.

The displayed reflection transfers this equation and uniqueness, and the distributional formula B_t extends bilinearly from L2×L2 into H^-2.

background_notes.justification: For Jref the coefficient is -hat f(-k), so reindexing preserves every even weighted squared norm and applying it twice returns f. The group multiplier has modulus one and conjugate values at opposite frequencies. For fixed f its coefficient differences tend to zero and their squared weighted sum has tail bounded by four times the norm tail, proving strong continuity. Combine this with continuity of u to obtain continuity of S_-t u(t). Multiplication of each integrated Fourier equation by exp(-itk^3) cancels its linear derivative term; the remaining term is exactly B_t(v,v)/2. The H^-2 estimate in S004 justifies its distributional interpretation.
